title: Kajabi Pricing 2026: Basic, Growth and Pro Plans
summary: Kajabi pricing offers tiered plans with different limits on contacts, products and users. Compare costs and find the tier that matches your needs.
body_markdown:
## Connecting Kajabi to Your Other Tools with Activepieces


Once you know which plan clears your limit, the next question is whether Kajabi's data can reach the rest of your business. Activepieces, **an automation tool that moves information between apps** , is one way to do that without changing what you pay Kajabi.


> If a cheaper plan's fee, cap or seat count would cost you more than the difference in price, the dearer plan is the cheaper one for you.


It doesn't lower Kajabi's price, raise a cap or stand in for a plan.


Your contacts, products and admin seats are still counted by Kajabi, so a workflow tool can't get you under a limit you've already crossed. Its job starts after the plan is chosen.


### When Kajabi's built-in integrations are enough


If a new purchase or signup only needs to land in one email tool Kajabi already connects to, use that connection and stop. It's one less thing to maintain, and when something breaks you have one vendor to call instead of two.


For small teams that check Kajabi's own reports once a week, the position is the same. Adding a second tool to solve a problem you don't have is how a tidy bill turns into two bills.


### What a workflow tool adds on top


The trouble starts when one sale needs to show up in several places. A buyer signs up, and someone has to add them to a customer list (a CRM), log the sale in a spreadsheet, and put them on the right email sequence.


Done by hand, that's copy-and-paste work that gets skipped on busy days, and a skipped step means a buyer who never gets the welcome email.


Here is how the route runs: Kajabi sends the purchase or signup through Activepieces, which passes it on to the CRM, the spreadsheet and the email tool in one pass. You set the rule once and the copying happens every time after.


There are two ways for Activepieces to listen for Kajabi. If its documentation lists a Kajabi connector, you pick it from a menu and choose the event.


If it doesn't, Kajabi can send a webhook, which is a message fired automatically when something happens, and Activepieces can catch that message.


The connector list is the` packages/pieces/community` folder of Activepieces'[MIT-licensed open-source monorepo on GitHub](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/tree/main/packages/pieces/community) , which holds 747 integrations, roughly 60% of them contributed by the community.


If a Kajabi connector isn't in that folder, the gap doesn't have to wait on anyone's roadmap: an integration can be generated for it and kept on your own instance, so the webhook is a fallback rather than your only route.


Before you commit, also check how Activepieces charges for the volume of runs you expect. That's a second limit to price, the same way you priced Kajabi's.


Activepieces is the better fit for Kajabi users whose other tools fall outside what Kajabi's built-in integrations cover, judged on how far the connection catalogue can stretch.


Kajabi's own limits on contacts, products and admin seats stay with Kajabi, and no workflow tool changes that, so this is a verdict about reach rather than price.


Because Activepieces' catalogue is open-source and can be counted directly from its monorepo, a missing connector is something you or the community can build, which makes its catalogue a floor and not a ceiling.
